title: Three teeth: س ش

bigIdea.text: س (sin) and ش (shin) share one body with three small teeth. No dots = 's'. Three dots above = 'sh'.

proper.text: The body is three small teeth in a row; standing alone or at the end of a word it also has a round tail below the line. ش has three dots above, like ث. In joined writing the teeth can be shallow, so count the bumps and check for dots.

Sounds: س is a clean 's' as in 'sun': the tongue tip near the front teeth with a narrow gap, so the air whistles. ش is 'sh' as in 'ship': the middle of the tongue rises toward the roof of the mouth and the air spreads out.
Sifat: both are 'whispered' (hams: the breath flows) and 'soft' (rakhawa: the sound flows). س has a 'whistle' (safir), like ص and ز. ش has 'spreading' (tafashshi): its air spreads through the mouth.

proper.text: Heavy or light: both are light. Neither is one of the seven heavy letters (خ ص ض غ ط ق ظ).

Common mistakes. Persian/Urdu readers: ص and ث are read like س, so three letters merge; keep this plain 's' for س only (ص and ث get their own lessons). English speakers reading transliteration: an 's' between vowels is not 'z' (as in 'rose'); س is always 's'. Everyone: keep س light next to heavy letters so it does not slide toward ص.

points.detail: Tip of the tongue with the front teeth (shared with ص and ز)
Middle of the tongue (shared with ج and ي)

memoryHook.text: Three teeth: add three dots and 's' becomes 'sh'.

extras.text: ث and ش both carry three dots above, on different bodies: a boat for ث, three teeth for ش.

tip.text: س: tongue tip near the front teeth, a thin whistle. ش: the middle of the tongue rises and the air spreads wide, with no whistle.

questions.q: Are س and ش heavy or light?
explain: Right: neither is one of the seven heavy letters.
The heavy letters are خ ص ض غ ط ق ظ.
sin is light; its heavy partner is ص.
shin is light.

questions.q: A transliteration shows 's' between two vowels. How do you say س?
explain: Right: English spelling sometimes turns 's' into 'z'; Arabic sin never changes.
'z' is the letter ز.
'sh' is the letter ش.
sin is pronounced.

questions.q: Your س sounds deep and heavy next to a heavy letter. What fixes it?
options: Keep the back of the tongue low so it stays light
Raise the back of the tongue more
explain: Right: sin is light whatever its neighbours are.
Raising the back of the tongue turns it toward ص.
Rounding the lips does not make it lighter.
sin is not a bouncing letter.

questions.q: Which two letters BOTH carry three dots above?
explain: Right: a boat for tha, three teeth for shin.
ta has two dots.
nun has one dot.
ya has two dots below.

remnote: س (sin) == Three teeth, no dots; tip of the tongue with the front teeth; 's' with a whistle; light
ش (shin) == Three teeth, three dots above; middle of the tongue; 'sh' with the air spreading; light
Persian/Urdu fix for س == Keep the plain 's' for س; ص and ث are different sounds
